scenes.heading: SCD Type 3
scenes.narration: A Slowly Changing Dimension of Type 3 keeps limited history by storing previous values in extra columns.

scenes.heading: How Type 3 works
bullets: Add a column for the prior value alongside the current one.
Only the most recent change is retained.
Great for tracking a single before-and-after.
scenes.narration: Type 3 adds a companion column, such as previous_region beside current_region. When a value changes, the current becomes previous and the new value takes its place. You keep exactly one step of history without the row explosion of Type 2.

scenes.heading: A Type 3 attribute change
scenes.code:
UPDATE dim_employee
SET    prev_department = department,
       department      = 'Marketing',
       changed_at      = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE  employee_id = 'E55';
scenes.narration: This moves the old department into the prev_department column before setting the new one. There is still just one row per employee, so the table stays compact. But because only a single prior value fits, any earlier department is lost.

scenes.heading: Type 2 vs Type 3
scenes.narration: Type 2 records every version so you can reconstruct the whole timeline. Type 3 keeps just the previous value in a column, which is enough when you only care about the last transition. Pick Type 3 when a simple current-versus-prior comparison answers the business question.

scenes.text: SCD Type 3 stores a limited history in parallel columns, capturing a single before-and-after without adding rows.
scenes.narration: Reach for Type 3 when comparing the current value to just its immediate predecessor is all the history you need.
